Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Are there different versions of the Quran?

The Quran is recited today in several recognised ways. What they are, how much they differ, what they show.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation.

Quran · Al-Muzzammil 73:4

Translation

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go. This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

Original · Hebrew

רַק֩ חֲזַ֨ק וֶֽאֱמַ֜ץ מְאֹ֗ד לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ כְּכָל־הַתּוֹרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוְּךָ֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדִּ֔י אַל־תָּס֥וּר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֔יל בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃ לֹֽא־יָמ֡וּשׁ סֵפֶר֩ הַתּוֹרָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה מִפִּ֗יךָ וְהָגִ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּי־אָ֛ז תַּצְלִ֥יחַ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֖ךָ וְאָ֥ז תַּשְׂכִּֽיל׃ הֲל֤וֹא צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַֽל־תַּעֲרֹ֖ץ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּ֤י עִמְּךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

Joshua · 1:7-9

World English Bible

﴿وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَـٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَـٰهُ تَنزِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [it is] a Qur’ān which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down progressively.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:106

Walk into a mosque in Jakarta, Lagos or Istanbul and you hear recitation in Arabic, learned from a teacher who learned it from a teacher. It is not read from a screen first; it is heard. In many places someone teaches children and adults this way, by voice, sitting beside them. The recitation is a living practice you can listen to today, not only a document in a library.

A question for you

What do you think a spoken tradition keeps that a printed one does not?

If you sayThe sound and the rhythm.
ThenYes, and in the Quran's case the sound is part of what the text is.
If you sayA person who can correct you.
ThenThat is the point of the chain of teachers: someone who listens and says again.
If you sayNothing special.
ThenFair. The next parts look at what the recognised ways of reciting actually differ in.

Part 2 of 3

﴿بَلْ هُوَ قُرْءَانٌ مَّجِيدٌ٢١ فِى لَوْحٍ مَّحْفُوظٍۭ٢٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

But this is an honored Qur’ān [Inscribed] in a Preserved Slate.

Quran · Al-Buruj 85:21-22

Here is a small, concrete case. In one verse the Quran is described as glorious and as being in a preserved tablet. Two recognised readings differ by one vowel: one makes ‘preserved’ describe the tablet, the other describes the Quran. Both are good Arabic, and both fit the written word. One text, a vowel apart. That is what a recognised reading is: a taught, regulated variation, not a different book.

A question for you

When is a variation a different book, and when is it a different way of reading the same one?

If you sayWhen the written text itself differs.
ThenThat is the line scholars draw: recognised readings must fit an early written text, with a small set of spelling differences in a few places.
If you sayWhen the meaning changes.
ThenThen look at the few places where it does. They are known, listed and studied, and many are read as complementary.
If you sayI need another example.
ThenFair. The Corpus Coranicum project lists readings with their attributed readers, so anyone can look at more.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?

Quran · Al-Qamar 54:17

Translation

For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֚י הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם לֹֽא־נִפְלֵ֥את הִוא֙ מִמְּךָ֔ וְלֹ֥א רְחֹקָ֖ה הִֽוא׃ לֹ֥א בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֤נוּ הַשָּׁמַ֨יְמָה֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃ וְלֹֽא־מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲבָר־לָ֜נוּ אֶל־עֵ֤בֶר הַיָּם֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃ כִּֽי־קָר֥וֹב אֵלֶ֛יךָ הַדָּבָ֖ר מְאֹ֑ד בְּפִ֥יךָ וּבִֽלְבָבְךָ֖ לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 30:11-14

World English Bible

How much do the readings differ? No count is offered here: no source this app has seen draws one from a full listing of the places. What scholars say: mostly pronunciation, vowelling and some details of spelling. In a few places the meaning is touched, and the two readings are often read as complementary. In the tenth century Ibn Mujahid chose seven readings already widely taught. Each is taught with its chain of teachers back to the Prophet, and Muslim scholars hold that many transmitted them in every generation.

A question for you

What would you most want to look at yourself?

If you sayThe manuscripts, to see the written text.
ThenThe previous Step looks at them, with their dates and their differences.
If you sayThe readings, to see exactly where they differ.
ThenThe Corpus Coranicum project lists variant readings with the readers they are attributed to. Anyone can look.
If you sayThe history of how the readings were chosen.
ThenIn the tenth century Ibn Mujahid chose seven readings already widely taught. Each still comes with its chain of teachers back to the Prophet.
